expectations.text: Does not claim to read every ticket/interview exhaustively
expectations.evidence: 'Deliberately did NOT open the support tickets, interviews, or other docs.'
No mention of subagents anywhere; single-agent quick check.
No file output beyond the report; response offers to go deeper, doesn't build anything.

expectations.text: Final response to the user is concise, not a full report
expectations.evidence: Response is roughly 180 words, three short paragraphs.

expectations.text: Checks the existing CLAUDE.md working-context file before proceeding
expectations.evidence: 'Checked the project root CLAUDE.md for prior findings... blank Module 1 placeholder.'

expectations.text: States an explicit confidence score distinguishing magnitude from causal certainty
expectations.evidence: No numeric confidence anywhere. Response uses qualitative language only ('not a five-alarm fire,' 'worth a quick look') and doesn't separate how sure it is that something's wrong from how sure it is about the cause.

claims.claim: Acceptance rate is recovering and not a crisis
claims.evidence: Only looked at the aggregate weekly rate (54%→73%), which the with-skill run's per-responder split shows is misleading — several responders are at or near zero, not 'recovering.' This claim is directionally softer than the evidence actually supports.

suggestions.assertion: States an explicit confidence score distinguishing magnitude from causal certainty
suggestions.reason: Both runs were restrained in scope, which is good, but only the with-skill run's extra discipline (splitting confidence by claim) caught that the aggregate recovery narrative is misleading. Worth considering whether a 'check per-entity variance, not just the aggregate' nudge belongs in the skill even for lightweight checks, since it's what produced the sharper, more correct read here.

eval_feedback.overall: Passes restraint checks but the lack of explicit confidence-splitting let a softer, less accurate read through uncaught.
